notes:
Summary: mid-market ITSM vendor building an internal helpdesk chatbot for enterprise customers. Primary goal: fast, accurate triage + immediate agent handoff.

Evaluation path: started with Hosted API for quick POC; if latency/cost/controls meet bar, they will evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit). Want turnkey streaming + tool calling for ticket ops (page engineers, create tickets, run lookups).

Key technical requirements: p95 end-user token latency target: <250ms for streaming-first-byte under typical load; ability to stream partial answers and call out to internal tools (ticket create, search). Prefers models with deterministic reranking for suggested KB articles.

Security & compliance: Okta SAML SSO required for console and admin; audit logs for all chat sessions with 90-day retention as baseline; ability to purge records on request; KMS integration mandatory for encryption at rest; regional residency requested for EU customers (future requirement).

POC notes: using internal KB (Confluence export) + recent Slack logs as seed prompts. Observed memory/KV cache savings when using prefix caching — SE recommended cache policy. Legal flagged DPA KMS clause and standard data residency wording; security team ran quick SOC2 checklist.

Quote from Head of Product: "We need answers fast — even a 100ms wobble shows up in metrics; streaming start is critical."

Staging constraints: initial rollout internal-only (agents + L1 support), must not send logs to third-party without encryption and retention controls.

Next steps (detailed): finish hosted POC, run sustained latency test (simulate 150 RPS internal traffic), deliver price worksheet for Dedicated headroom vs. burst. Slack webhook for tool calls to be demoed in POC week 2. Legal to review DPA & KMS addendum.

Potential win criteria: p95 streaming-first-byte <=250ms, page/create-ticket tool calls complete <500ms, SOC2-friendly telemetry (audit logs + ability to export), committed price within $75k-$125k ARR equivalent.
